summary:
Simple probing on an equation (R1, milestone M2) is built, committed on branch stage1c-m2 (three commits, head edd147a7e) and meets the local form of every criterion; one wrong reduction of my own rule was found by the campaign on the way and repaired, and one defect of the base engine was found and is reported, not repaired.

What exists: the family simple_probing_t on its row list (balance test in O(1), one scan for the binaries, one scan per binary tried, gaps as differences of the compensated sums); src/forcing.hpp, the forcing test as one function that the forcing row and simple probing call; src/alias_apply.hpp, the alias batch that the doubleton equations and simple probing share (a row is deleted only when all its edges became maps, a row with a cut edge stays, and its alias then names no row); the generator knob p_probing_row with its variants, gprs_fuzz --probing; fixed models 7 and 10; eleven wrong engines (the five named and six more); the family in the events driver, the fixed-point tests and the end-to-end profiles. No new record kind.

Verified: 495 tests pass in both builds on the committed tree (473 before). With the family off the engine is identical with the base commit model by model, phase hashes included, on the 17 local dumps, the 240 local dumps and 4.2 million random models, each in both builds. Campaign on the final engine: 163.2 million models in the release build and 51 million in the assertion build, no oracle failure, no structure failure, no second presolve that changes a fixed point. All 110 wrong engines are caught. Check tool without a solver: no failed verdict on the 17 local dumps (both modes) and on the 240 local dumps (both modes). On the 240 local dumps the engine stands at 1.0021 / 1.0023 / 1.0023 of the reference m2_a in nonzeros / rows / columns (237 instances), no instance is larger than before in either mode, and the time is +2.2%.

The wrong reduction I found and repaired (commit 9d7b5aa0f): a continuous column whose two bounds were rounding apart got an alias whose scale was that rounding, which put coefficients of 2e-15 into another row and cut off feasible points. It showed on 6 of 20.4 million release models and 2 of 10.2 million assertion models, all with --columns and a random subset of families without the row rules. The rule now leaves such a row; every long run was repeated on the repaired engine.

Not done: nothing with a solver, nothing on the node or the 44 testbed instances, no solution-quality measurement of any assumption. The base engine's defect on coefficients of 1e7 (singleton row of an integer column) is not repaired.
design:
Choices where the design left room.
1. One batch per call. The call visits its listed rows, collects the rows that pass, and applies the batch after the last visit, so every test reads one state. A row whose columns the batch already connects is pushed back on the family's own list at once (it can have no event: both connected columns can end as roots).
2. Work: line_visit_work per visited row, the used slots of the row per scan, the used slots of a column that is read for the size test (once per call, cached), and for a row that enters the batch the live entries of its columns. The budget is tested between two rows only.
3. Findings count one per alias, as the doubleton family counts.
4. The alias depth comes from a new array alias_forest_t::depth that freeze() fills; alias_map_t is unchanged.
5. Statistics of the family in column_stats_t (rows in a batch, deleted, left with a cut edge, visits left for each of five reasons, calls with a depth above 1, entry changes, largest scale), in the JSON of gprs_presolve (object "probing") and in a line "probing" of gprs_fuzz that run_campaign.sh sums.
6. Eleven wrong engines instead of five: sp_dir, sp_gap, sp_range, sp_cont, sp_row as named, and sp_cut, sp_named, sp_unit, sp_size, sp_limited, sp_narrow for the code the design does not name.

Deviations from the design, with the reason.
a. The binary must have the bounds 0 and 1, and so must every other integer column of the row with bounds one apart (the design: upper - lower == 1 exactly). Reason: only such columns can be a root or lie between a column and its root; with bounds 7 and 8 on a root the offsets of all aliases below it are rounded differences multiplied by a scale of up to 1e6. With 0 and 1 the offset of any alias is a bound of its own column, whichever root the forest picks. Cost on the 240 local dumps: no visit is left for it.
b. Three limits the design does not have. (i) Rounding: a row with a continuous column whose range is not far above the rounding of its bounds, or of the row, is left. This is the repair of the wrong reduction that the campaign found (model in the commit message of 9d7b5aa0f and as a test). (ii) Size of an offset: max(|lower|, |upper|) of a column times its largest coefficient must stay within tol.feasibility / tol.side_error (1e8), and every finite side of a row of the column must be readable, because the offset enters those sides. This test reads other rows, which change without an event of the visited row, so a row left for it makes the call report limited. (iii) The side of the row itself must be readable.
c. alias_scale_limit is an option of options_t (it was a named constant in rules.hpp), and the tolerance of the balance test is the option probing_balance; both because of the owner's rule on assumptions.
d. Fixed model 7 as the design states it (second row 1000 x1 >= 1.5e-4) cannot catch sp_cont through the engine: the second row is a singleton row, the cascade makes the bound of x1 explicit before the rule runs, and the wrong alias then fits. The literal model is kept as a direct call of the family; the oracle part uses a second row with two columns and a side that is off by 4e-10, so that only the forcing test stands between the row and the alias.
e. sp_range needs two replacements. With the gap tests as the design writes them, an integer column of range 2 can never pass (the two gap tests imply a range below 2), so a wrong engine that only drops the range test is the right engine. The wrong engine takes a column of range 2 whose term carries half the range, which is what the generator variant draws.
f. The balance test is written as the design says (one tolerance, error bounds subtracted). It is stricter than the two forcing tests by themselves, which allow two tolerances.
g. Citations: the design cites an older tree. At the base commit substitute() and the batch loop are at src/rules_doubleton.cpp:113-156 and 208-239 (design: 108-160, 212-243), the edge test at src/alias_forest.cpp:41-70 (design: 44-57), the forest contract at include/gprs/postsolve.hpp:270-315 (design: 149-169), the round at src/presolve.cpp:338-367 (design: 265-288), and check/structure_check.hpp has 2076 lines where the design cites a file of 1062. rules_rows.cpp:152-180 and HPresolve.cpp:2696-2698 agree. I followed the code.
h. The six wrong engines of the doubleton family and three objective ones (obj_alias_abs, obj_cancel_wide, obj_offset_scale) follow the code to src/alias_apply.hpp and now act on simple probing too; r_forcing follows the forcing test to src/forcing.hpp with the same behaviour.

evidence:
All runs are on this Mac, with at most 5 processes of mine. The engine sources have not changed since commit 9d7b5aa0f; the release binary rebuilt from the final commit has the same SHA-256 (9923e92f...) as the one that made every measurement below.

1. Tests. 495 tests pass in the assertion build and in the release build, rebuilt from the committed tree (473 at the base; 20 new in tests/test_columns_probing.cpp, 2 new in tests/test_engine_fixed_point.cpp).

2. Identity with the family off, against the base engine built from fa8430e24, with a driver that prints per model the reduced-model hash, the stack hashed field by field, the fixed-point flag, rounds, rebuilds, dual findings, the statistics (calls, work, first work, findings, records, removals) of every family but simple_probing, the column statistics, and a hash over the phase hashes (state and stack after every phase). New-off against base-off with phase hashes, and new-off against base-on (the base's empty family) without them:
- 17 local dumps, 8 option variants each (default, primal-only, rebuild always, rebuild never, tiny budgets, two rounds, no propagation, doubleton and dual fixing only): 136 lines per build, 0 differ in the release and in the assertion build.
- 240 local dumps, the same 8 variants: 1,920 lines per build, 0 differ in both builds.
- Random models: 4.2 million per build (12 profiles times 35,000 seeds, with no profile option, --singletons, --columns, --probing, --probing --singletons; once with the options of the seed, 2.1 million, and once forced into primal-only mode, 2.1 million): 0 of 4,200 chunks of 1,000 models differ in either build.
- The stored run: results/bench240/s1c_m2_mac/off against results/bench240/s1c_m1_mac/default on the 240: hash, rounds, flag, status and calls, work, findings of every other family equal on all 240.

3. Wrong engines: 110 (99 existing, 11 new), make_mutants.py run on the committed tree, all apply. Each ran on 1.2 million release models (20,000 seeds times 12 profiles times 5 option sets). 96 are caught by a campaign check. The other 14 fail unit tests named for them: the nine that M1 reported as unit-test only (fs_guard, zs_guard, fc_guard, fs_drift, r_alias_drift, fs_shared, fs_limited, ev_sides, ev_scale), ev_unread, and sp_cont, sp_size, sp_limited, sp_narrow.
- The six doubleton ones on the moved code: r_dbl_bounds (oracle 1,461, structure 2,161), r_dbl_side (10,781 / 4,905), r_dbl_scale (4,927 / 2,599), r_dbl_cost (17,091 / 16,765 objective), r_dbl_objoff (22,329 / 23,624 objective), r_alias_offset (44,693 / 46,687). r_forcing 19,991 / 11,512 and second presolve 330; r_forcing_end 58,429 / 46,240.
- The five named: sp_dir oracle 2,690 and structure rows 2,518; sp_gap oracle 15, structure rows 14; sp_range oracle 550, structure rows 458; sp_row oracle 1,748, structure rows 2,255; sp_cont no campaign check, as the design says, and the fixed model through the oracle (columns_probing_leaves_a_continuous_column_that_is_off_its_bound) plus the tolerance test.
- The six more: sp_cut oracle 3, structure rows 5; sp_named structure stack 1 and two unit tests; sp_unit oracle 1,055, structure rows 374; sp_size, sp_limited, sp_narrow one unit test each.
- ev_unread and ev_scale, as asked, on 4.8 million release models each with --columns and with --probing: ev_unread is caught by the second presolve, 6 of 4.8 million with --columns (M1's seed 9300036821 among them) and 1 of 4.8 million with --probing; that one stays with simple probing switched off, so it is the singleton family that misses the event. ev_scale is caught by no campaign check (0 of 9.6 million); it fails 5 unit tests, ev_unread 9. Simple probing gives neither a new way to show: it reads equations only, whose two sides are finite, so every bound change of their columns is a read activity event, and it has no column list.

4. Campaign on the final engine, 5 processes, first seeds 9.0e9 to 10.4e9. No oracle failure, no structure failure, no second presolve that changes a fixed point in any of the twelve runs.
Release, 20.4 million models each (results with a probing alias / rows deleted / rows left with a cut edge / calls with an alias depth above 1): --probing 260,974 / 263,194 / 459 / 80,538; --probing --singletons 146,574 / 147,474 / 113 / 44,877; --columns 4,140 / 4,143 / 0 / 2,556; --singletons 2,758 / 2,760 / 0 / 1,902; no profile 1,291 / 1,291 / 0 / 843. Two more: --columns on other seeds, 40.8 million models, 8,373 / 8,393 / 0 / 5,128; --probing --columns, 20.4 million, 337,974 / 340,914 / 532 / 104,135. Release total 163.2 million models, 17.4 million second presolves of a fixed point, 1,694,688 probing aliases of which 1,193 name no row, largest depth 4.
Assertion build, 10.2 million each: --probing 129,979 / 131,112 / 227 / 40,029; --probing --singletons 73,478 / 73,898 / 53 / 22,480; --columns 2,084 / 2,089 / 0 / 1,277; --singletons 1,379 / 1,379 / 0 / 935; no profile 613 / 613 / 0 / 393. Total 51 million, 5.3 million second presolves.
Visits left in the release runs: columns connected 306,442; bounds one apart that are not 0 and 1: 607,630; scale limit 88,440 (reached through the option draw that sets the limit to 2); rounding 45; size of an offset 2,126.
None of the known seeds of classes (a) and (b) lies in these seed ranges, and no failure of those classes appeared.
Before the repair the same five option sets gave 6 oracle failures in the release --columns run and 2 in the assertion --columns run, all the rounding case; the other eight runs were clean. Log: chain1_before_fix.log.

5. Check tool without a solver (LP and MIP limits 0). 17 local dumps, default and primal-only, 2 cost variants, 4 pushed points: 34 results, 980 verdicts pass, 352 skipped (the solver verdicts), none failed. 240 local dumps, both modes, 2 cost variants, no points: 240 results, exit code 0 on all, 5,040 verdicts pass, 4,320 skipped, none failed; no row, kept row, added row, bound, box, snapshot, objective or postsolve failure in either mode.

6. A base-engine defect found on the way, not of this rule and not repaired: with the generator switch probing_wide (coefficients and sides of 1e7 among the small integers; off in every campaign above) 7 of 480,000 release models fail the oracle, and the same 7 fail with simple probing off. Traced on one: a singleton row with an integer column and a coefficient of 1e7 rounds the bound with the feasibility tolerance in the units of the column (x1 = 10000004 / 10000010.67 = 0.99999933 is taken as 1) and the row is deleted with a violation of 6.67. Reproducer: probe/base_big.cpp in my scratch directory, and gprs_fuzz --probing-wide.

assumptions.title: The binary has the bounds 0 and 1
assumptions.statement: Only an integer column with bounds exactly 0 and 1 is taken as the binary, and a row that holds another integer column with bounds one apart that are not 0 and 1 is left. The design takes any integer column with upper - lower == 1.
assumptions.alternatives: Any integer column with bounds one apart, as the design and HiGHS (which allows the feasibility tolerance); this needs a bound on the rounded offsets under composition, which I did not find without changing the alias forest.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 visits left for it. Campaign, 163.2 million release models: 607,630 visits left for it.

assumptions.title: Limit on the scale of an alias
assumptions.statement: Every other column of the row has upper - lower <= 1e6; beyond it the row is left.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: the largest scale applied is 1 and no visit is left; with --alias-scale-limit 1 the reduced-model hash is the same on all 240. So any limit of 1 or more gives the same result there.

assumptions.title: Tolerance of the balance test
assumptions.statement: A row is scanned only when |(M - b) - (b - m)| less the two error bounds is at most one feasibility tolerance. The two forcing tests by themselves allow two.
assumptions.alternatives: 2, which makes the balance test a pure filter of the forcing tests.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: with 2 the reduced-model hash is the same on all 240 (277,320 findings both ways).

assumptions.title: Tolerance of the two forcing tests
assumptions.statement: Each conditional row is forcing in the engine's sense: the gap within tol.feasibility * min|a| / max(1, max|a|) over the entries other than the binary, and with a continuous column among them positive only by the error bound of the activity plus 8 rounding units of the terms.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::feasibility, and the named constant forcing_rounding_units = 8 that the forcing row shares
assumptions.alternatives: HiGHS's absolute 1e-9 on the balance and on the coefficient.

assumptions.title: A continuous column whose range is rounding is left
assumptions.statement: A row is left when a continuous column of it has bound_rounding(lower) + bound_rounding(upper) above tol.zero times its range, or when the positive part of a gap (with its error bound) is above tol.zero times the smallest |a| * range among its continuous columns.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::zero = 1e-9
assumptions.alternatives: No such test is wrong (found by the campaign). Another factor than tol.zero; treating such a column as a constant of the row instead of leaving the row.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 visits left for it. Campaign: 45 in 163.2 million release models. Without it: 6 oracle failures in 20.4 million release models with --columns, 2 in 10.2 million in the assertion build.

assumptions.title: Size of an offset
assumptions.statement: For the binary and every other column, max(|lower|, |upper|) times the largest coefficient of the column, times tol.side_error, must not exceed tol.feasibility (so the product is at most 1e8), and every finite side of a row of the column must be readable. A row left for this alone makes the call report limited.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::side_error = 1e-14 and tolerances_t::feasibility
assumptions.alternatives: No such test, as the doubleton equations have none; a test of exactness of each shifted side instead of a size.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 visits left for it, so no fixed-point flag is lost. Campaign: 2,126 visits in 163.2 million release models.

assumptions.title: The side of the row is readable and no activity term is infinite
assumptions.statement: A row is visited only when its side b has |b| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility and neither activity holds an infinite term (above tol.infinite_term).
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::side_error, tolerances_t::infinite_term

assumptions.title: Explicit bounds only
assumptions.statement: Activities are over explicit bounds; a recorded implied bound is never read (design).
assumptions.alternatives: Implied bounds, as HiGHS reads them.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: neos-1445765 gets 18,444 aliases, HiGHS's count, in the first round; highschool1-aigio, neos-1445765, bab2, bab6 and the two cryptanalysis instances end at the reference's sizes, brazil3 and academictimetablesmall below them. No instance shows a loss.

assumptions.title: One batch per call; a connected row waits
assumptions.statement: A row is taken into the batch only when no two of its free columns are connected by the batch already; otherwise it goes back on the list for the next call (design).
assumptions.alternatives: Serving the list until it stays empty inside one call.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 952 visits wait, 476 on each cryptanalysis instance; both end at the reference's sizes. Campaign: 306,442 in 163.2 million release models.

assumptions.title: Order of the binaries
assumptions.statement: The columns that can be the binary are tried in increasing column index and the first that passes every limit is taken.
assumptions.measured: not measured; two binaries can both pass only when coefficients are at the size of the tolerance

assumptions.title: Budget of the family
assumptions.statement: 4 passes, 2 stall passes, floor 100,000 work units per call (design).
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: the family uses at most 0.80 passes in its first call and 0.69 in all later calls together; the campaign draws tiny budgets for one seed in ten.

assumptions.title: Place in the round
assumptions.statement: Once per round, after the doubleton equations and before the singleton columns (design).

assumptions.title: On in primal-only mode
assumptions.statement: The rule runs in primal-only mode: every feasible point satisfies the aliases (design, class B/S).
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, primal-only: the same 277,320 aliases; 1.0103 / 1.0105 / 1.0219 against the engine before in that mode.

assumptions.title: An alias names its row only when the batch deleted it
assumptions.statement: A probing alias carries its row when all edges of the row became maps and the row was deleted, else -1 (amendment D, validity item 5).
assumptions.alternatives: none (the other reading fails the structure check on a correct result)
assumptions.measured: Campaign: 1,193 of 1,694,688 probing aliases name no row in the release runs; 0 on the 240 local dumps.

assumptions.title: Generator and campaign draws
assumptions.statement: gprs_fuzz --probing sets p_probing_row = 0.7 and max_probing_rows = 3; the binary is a 0/1 column nine times in ten; three seeds in eight change a setting (alias_scale_limit 2, alias_scale_limit 1e8, probing_balance 2). probing_wide (coefficients of 1e7) is off.
assumptions.where: tests/oracle.hpp:149-175; tests/oracle.cpp (probing rows); tools/gprs_fuzz.cpp:262-268 and the end of variant()
assumptions.measured: With --probing 1.3% of the models get a probing alias (260,974 of 20.4 million). With --probing-wide 7 of 480,000 models fail, and the same 7 with simple probing off.

unsure: The rounding test is my repair of a case the campaign showed at 3 in 10 million models with one option set. The two thresholds (tol.zero against the rounding of the bounds, and against the term range) are chosen by argument, not by measurement; after the repair 45 visits were left for it in 163.2 million release models and no failure appeared, but the generator reaches this case only when the row rules are switched off, so its coverage is thin.

The same hazard, a difference of two rounded bounds used as a scale, is open for the single-lock alias of M4 (scale = upper - lower) and should be looked at for the parallel-column rules. I did not check whether the doubleton equations can meet it; there the scale is a ratio of coefficients, not a difference of bounds.

The size test for an offset is stricter than anything the doubleton equations do and makes the call report limited. It leaves nothing on the 240 local dumps, but instances with bounds or sides beyond 1e8 next to a probing row would lose the reduction and the fixed-point flag.

The claim that only 0/1 integer columns can be a root or an inner node of a tree of the batch rests on my reading of the root choice in alias_forest_t::freeze (a column next to a binary never scores above that binary); it is not asserted in the code. The campaign covers it only through the oracle.
Timing was measured under a load average of 6 to 9 from other work; +2.2% on the 240 local dumps and +0.5% on the 17 are good to a few percent.

for_next_milestone: src/alias_apply.hpp is the shared batch: alias_batch_t (init(st), add(edge), clear()), apply_aliases(st, ps, tol, batch, origin, budget, result), tree_of(forest, col), plus transfer_bounds, substitute and set_root_slots. The caller spends the work when it collects an edge; apply_aliases does not test the budget and counts one finding per map.

Trap for the single-lock alias (R8, M4): apply_aliases deletes a row once every edge that the row gave has become a map. The lock row must stay. Either give add() a way not to count the edge, or keep open_edges[row] one above its edges so it never reaches zero; the record then gets row = -1 by itself (substitute passes the row only when it is dead), which is what push_alias asserts for origin lock.

R8 needs the same three guards that simple probing has, and they live in the anonymous namespace of src/rules_simple_probing.cpp: is_unit (bounds 0 and 1; R8's design already asks for this), reach / offset_fits (size of the offset against the rows of the column, cached per call, reports limited) and the rounding test for a continuous column (its scale is upper - lower too). Move them to a shared header when R8 is built. Without the rounding test R8 will make the wrong reduction that this milestone found.
src/forcing.hpp has forcing_entries_t, forcing_possible and forcing(). R8's force test for a continuous column must use it (amendment D, validity item 6).
options_t::alias_scale_limit is now an option (default 1e6); R8 reads opt.alias_scale_limit. options_t::probing_balance is new.
alias_forest_t::depth (by position in touched, set by freeze) gives the maps composed between a column and its root; column_stats_t::alias_depth is the largest per call of simple probing.

For dominance between parallel columns (R6, M3) nothing new is prepared beyond src/implied.hpp; src/parallel_keys.hpp is not built, and src/rules_parallel_rows.cpp, from which it is to come, is being changed by the repair of known failure (c) in another worktree. R6's ratio and R9's merged bounds are also numbers made from data of the state; check them against bounds that are rounding apart.
